parsed.rationale: On this tracing alone I see sinus rhythm at about 65 bpm with normal PR and narrow QRS. V2–V3 show only about 1 mm of concave J-point elevation with a normal-looking T wave, below the 2 mm STEMI threshold, and I see no reciprocal ST depression, Q waves or bundle branch block. If the patient was diagnosed with STEMI, this was probably an early or pre-infarction ECG, or hyperacute T waves that are too subtle to call from one image, so serial ECGs are needed.
